summary: This article explains how museums collect, preserve, research, and display objects so people can learn about the past, how curators decide what to show, and an example from the National Museum in Riyadh.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Museums: Keepers of History”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a person who decides what a museum will show and explains it to visitors
a group of objects arranged together for people to see
to protect something carefully so it lasts a long time

challengeTerms.def: the careful work of protecting something so it is not damaged or lost
the history of where something came from and who has owned it
to explain the meaning of something so other people can understand it

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that museums are one of the best ways to learn about history? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a curator and research work together to create a museum exhibit.
struggling: Pre-teach curator, exhibit, and preserve with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses conservation, provenance, and interpret to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
